title: Methylmalonic acidaemia (MMA)
summary: Methylmalonic acidaemia means the body cannot break down some parts of protein and fat. A substance called methylmalonic acid builds up and can make a person unwell, often from the first days of life.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the same gene (most often MMUT) from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has MMA. How it affects someone depends on the exact type. It is managed for life with a special diet and close care from a specialist team.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has MMA. Could I be a carrier?
What does a test for MMA involve?
card_summary: The body can't break down some parts of protein and fat. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Managed for life by a specialist team with a special diet.
care: Specialist metabolic and kidney clinics, dietitians, genetic counselling and family support groups.
